standard.title: Social conventions and turn-taking
standard.description: understand that cooperation with others depends on shared understanding of social conventions, including turn-taking patterns, acknowledgement and body language
standard.prior_knowledge: Students investigate how language choices vary according to context and roles in interaction (AC9E2LA01). They have not yet examined the specific conventions — turn-taking, acknowledgement, body language — that enable cooperation in group situations.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students understand that cooperation depends on shared social conventions including turn-taking patterns, acknowledgement and body language.

nodes.label: Turn-taking and collaborative language
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can identify turn-taking conventions and collaborative language in group and pair work, and explain how they enable cooperation.
nodes.minimum_width: Identify at least two collaborative language conventions (e.g. initiating, inviting, responding) and explain how they help a group work together.
nodes.typical_width: Recognise and use collaborative language for initiating, inviting, responding and extending in group and pair work; explain how turn-taking patterns and language choices support cooperative interaction.
wider: Compare how turn-taking conventions differ across formal group discussions versus casual conversations, and explain why different contexts have different rules
Examine specific First Nations Australian cultural protocols and speaking/listening conventions, and discuss how understanding different conventions helps people cooperate respectfully

response_modes.reason: Students often see turn-taking as a single set of rules rather than as context-dependent conventions. Comparing different group contexts — and especially different cultural protocols — reveals that cooperation requires understanding which conventions apply in which situation.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: The First Nations Australian cultural protocols elaboration is explicitly named here, offering a genuinely enriching width direction. Understanding that different communities have different interaction conventions deepens the concept beyond classroom rules into respectful cultural awareness.
success_criteria: Student identifies at least two specific turn-taking or collaborative language conventions
Student explains how one convention helps people cooperate — not just that it's polite

nodes.label: Acknowledgement and body language
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can identify acknowledgement behaviours and body language that signal cooperation, and explain their role in shared understanding.
nodes.minimum_width: Identify at least one acknowledgement behaviour and one body language signal in an interaction and explain how each supports the interaction.
nodes.typical_width: Recognise how acknowledgement (e.g. nodding, verbal feedback, building on others' ideas) and body language (eye contact, orientation, gesture) signal engagement and cooperation in a range of interaction contexts.
wider: Discuss how body language conventions vary across cultures — identifying examples where the same gesture or behaviour has different meanings for different groups
Reflect on an interaction where miscommunication occurred and identify which conventions were unclear or differently understood
success_criteria: Student identifies an acknowledgement behaviour and a body language signal in an observed or enacted interaction
Student explains how these signals show that participants share understanding and are cooperating
